title: Repair a Boolean decision contract
instructions:
All commands and files for this exam belong on the initial controller. This is an unofficial practical exam, not an official OPA certification. There is one Kubernetes node, no context switching, and no prerequisite questions.

Work in `/opt/opa-workshop/q1`. Repair `policy.rego` so `data.q1.allow` is a defined Boolean: allow only when `input.user.department` is the string `finance` and `input.action` is `read`. Deny other actions, departments, missing fields, and unexpected types. Use Rego v1. For example, `{"user":{"department":"finance"},"action":"read"}` must allow. You may use `opa eval --data policy.rego --stdin-input data.q1.allow`.
steps: Keep package q1 and add default allow := false.
Conjoin the two equality checks in a single allow body.
Evaluate allowed, denied, and missing-field inputs.
solution:
cat > /opt/opa-workshop/q1/policy.rego <<'REGO'
package q1

default allow := false
allow if {
  input.user.department == "finance"
  input.action == "read"
}
REGO

checks.description: Decision path, Boolean fallback, and department/action boundary are correct

explanation: Packages determine the data query path; input remains the per-request document. A failed body produces no value, so a Boolean contract needs a fallback. A default does not populate missing input. See https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/policy-language

title: Enforce tenant-scoped reader permissions
instructions: In `/opt/opa-workshop/q2/policy.rego`, implement Boolean `data.q2.allow` with default denial. Load the supplied `data.json` containing `users` and `documents`; preserve it. Input contains `user` (user ID), `resource` (document ID), and `action`. Only `read` is permitted, only for a user whose trusted `roles` contains `reader`, and only when that user's trusted tenant equals the document's trusted tenant. Unknown users/documents or missing attributes must deny. Ignore caller-supplied `tenant`, `resource_tenant`, and `roles` claims. Alice may read doc:1 but not doc:2; Bob has the opposite scope; Eve has no reader role.
steps: Resolve the user and document from data using their IDs.
Require read, reader membership, and tenant equality in the same body.
Test a cross-tenant reader and forged caller claims.
solution:
cat > /opt/opa-workshop/q2/policy.rego <<'REGO'
package q2

default allow := false
allow if {
  input.action == "read"
  user := data.users[input.user]
  document := data.documents[input.resource]
  "reader" in user.roles
  user.tenant == document.tenant
}
REGO

checks.description: Trusted role and tenant checks allow legitimate reads and reject bypasses

explanation: Separate allow definitions are alternatives, not conjunctions. Comparing two client-controlled tenant claims proves no ownership. The fixture represents identity and resource data supplied by a trusted integration. See https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/external-data

title: Combine attributes with explicit suspension precedence
instructions: Implement `data.q3.allow` in `/opt/opa-workshop/q3/policy.rego`. Permit only `read`, with matching nonempty string departments at `input.subject.department` and `input.resource.department`, a `reader` role in the subject's roles array, and `input.subject.suspended` explicitly Boolean false. All other inputs must return Boolean false, without conflicts. A missing suspension attribute is not evidence of false. Input attributes are trusted by this task's integration; do not add external identity lookups.
steps: Start from default denial.
Check department types/nonemptiness, reader membership, and action.
Require suspended == false; test a suspended reader and missing suspension.
solution:
cat > /opt/opa-workshop/q3/policy.rego <<'REGO'
package q3

default allow := false
allow if {
  input.action == "read"
  is_string(input.subject.department)
  input.subject.department != ""
  input.subject.department == input.resource.department
  is_array(input.subject.roles)
  "reader" in input.subject.roles
  input.subject.suspended == false
}
REGO

checks.description: ABAC checks and explicit suspension precedence produce total Boolean decisions

explanation: Rego does not infer deny precedence from names or source order. Encode the combining logic explicitly. Negation-as-failure can succeed on absent data, while equality with false requires an actual false value. See https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/policy-language#negation

title: Collect all policy violations
instructions: In `/opt/opa-workshop/q4/policy.rego`, implement partial set `data.q4.violations`. Add exactly `missing-owner` when `input.owner` is absent or is not a nonempty string. Add exactly `public-access` when `input.public` is Boolean true. Return both when both conditions apply, and an empty set when neither applies. Missing or non-Boolean public values do not add public-access. The JSON representation of the result is an array; order is irrelevant. This question does not require an allow rule.
steps: Define a helper recognizing a nonempty string owner.
Use contains rules to collect independent messages.
Check zero, one, and two violations.
solution:
cat > /opt/opa-workshop/q4/policy.rego <<'REGO'
package q4

owner_valid if {
  is_string(input.owner)
  input.owner != ""
}
violations contains "missing-owner" if not owner_valid
violations contains "public-access" if input.public == true
REGO

checks.description: Violation collection has exact messages, including an empty set

explanation: Partial sets collect all successful heads and deduplicate their members. Zero matches produces an empty set, unlike an undefined complete rule. See https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/policy-language

title: Reject missing identities and vacuous approvals
instructions: Implement Boolean `data.q5.allow` in `/opt/opa-workshop/q5/policy.rego`. Require `input.user.admin` explicitly false and a nonempty array `input.approvals` in which every element has `accepted` explicitly true. Missing fields, wrong types, an empty list, or any rejected/malformed approval must deny. A mixture of accepted and rejected approvals must not allow.
steps: Compare admin to false instead of negating an absent reference.
Conjoin is_array, count > 0, and every in one body.
Test empty, mixed, missing, and all-accepted cases.

checks.description: Explicit false and nonempty universal approval requirements hold

explanation: Every is vacuously true on an empty collection. Nonemptiness is a separate conjunct. A second allow definition would make it an alternative rather than a requirement. See https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/policy-language#every-keyword

title: Write tests that catch authorization regressions
instructions: Write Rego v1 test rules in `/opt/opa-workshop/q6/tests.rego`, package `tenant_test`, importing `data.tenant.allow`. The trusted policy is `/opt/painkiller/opa001/testing/good.rego`; do not copy or redefine its decision. It allows only when role is reader AND tenant equals resource_tenant, with default false. Write at least four test_ rules covering: permitted same-tenant reader, cross-tenant reader denied, same-tenant non-reader denied, and missing attributes explicitly false. Use `with input as ...` to supply inputs. Run `opa test /opt/painkiller/opa001/testing/good.rego /opt/opa-workshop/q6/tests.rego`. Your tests must pass the correct implementation and fail implementations that omit either boundary, allow everything, deny everything, or omit default denial. Do not load the entire testing directory: it contains deliberately broken variants.
steps: Use an equality assertion for false, not merely not allow.
Keep unrelated conditions satisfied when testing each boundary.
Run against the correct policy and individually against the supplied mutants.

checks.description: Candidate tests pass the good policy and detect all five faulty variants

explanation: Coverage does not prove tenant isolation. Mutation testing supplies evidence that assertions detect specific defects. Explicit false assertions also distinguish undefined from a normal denial. See https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/policy-testing

title: Repair the enforcement point
instructions: Repair `/opt/opa-workshop/q7/adapter.py`, a Python 3 command-line enforcement adapter. It reads one JSON transport observation from stdin and writes only one JSON object to stdout: `{"allow":BOOLEAN,"reason":STRING}`. For `{"status":200,"body":{"result":true}}`, output true/allow. Explicit false gives false/deny; a successful object body with no result gives false/undefined; a present non-Boolean result or non-object body gives false/invalid; non-200 status gives false/error. An observation with `error:"timeout"` gives false/timeout; any other error gives false/error. Errors take precedence over status. Preserve these distinctions, never authorize on HTTP success alone, and do not perform network requests. This fixture isolates result interpretation; it does not implement authentication or a complete HTTP application.
steps: Inspect the result using Boolean identity, not truthiness.
Distinguish absent result, wrong type, HTTP error, and timeout.
Allow the protected operation only for the explicit true case.

checks.description: Adapter enforces explicit true and preserves denial/failure distinctions

explanation: OPA is the decision point, not the enforcement point. Data API success with no result represents undefined, not permission. A transport failure means no usable decision arrived. This exercise deliberately tests the adapter boundary independently. See https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/rest-api

title: Authorize directed relationship paths
instructions: Implement Boolean `data.q8.allow` in `/opt/opa-workshop/q8/policy.rego` using the supplied, unchanged `data.json` relationship graph and `graph.reachable`. Input has `user`, `resource`, and `action`. Permit only read, only for user alice or bob, only for resources whose IDs begin `doc:`, and only when reachable along the directed edges from that user. Alice reaches doc:7 through team:blue; Bob reaches doc:8 through team:green. Cross-team access, reverse paths, team objects, unknown users, missing fields, and writes must deny. Do not implement recursive Rego rules.
steps: Validate action, known principal, and document prefix.
Compute graph.reachable from a singleton set containing input.user.
Require the resource to be in the reachable set.
solution:
cat > /opt/opa-workshop/q8/policy.rego <<'REGO'
package q8

default allow := false
allow if {
  input.action == "read"
  input.user in {"alice", "bob"}
  startswith(input.resource, "doc:")
  reachable := graph.reachable(data.relationships, {input.user})
  input.resource in reachable
}
REGO

checks.description: Directed reachability grants only the intended document reads

explanation: Graph direction and edge provenance define the authorization model. Reachability includes the starting node, so constrain permitted resource types and principal identities. See https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/policy-reference/builtins/graph

title: Publish and activate a revisioned bundle
instructions: In `/opt/opa-workshop/q9/src`, implement `data.release.allow` allowing only read for users in supplied `data.release.readers` (alice and bob), with default false. Preserve the supplied readers data. Create `.manifest` with revision `release-1`, roots `["release"]`, and rego_version 1. Build `/opt/opa-workshop/q9/bundle.tar.gz` using `opa build --bundle ...`. The loopback workshop server serves this exact artifact at `http://127.0.0.1:18888/bundles/q9.tar.gz`; the already-running systemd unit `opa001-q9` queries it and exposes OPA at `http://127.0.0.1:18189`. Keep the release bundle configured in q9/config.yaml. Verify activation, not just download: status reports are visible at `http://127.0.0.1:18888/events/status/q9`. The active bundle must report revision release-1 and serve the intended Boolean decisions. Use `sudo systemctl restart opa001-q9` if needed.
steps: Write policy and manifest without placing per-request input in the bundle.
Build to the served artifact path.
Wait for polling and inspect status plus representative Data API decisions.
solution:
cat > /opt/opa-workshop/q9/src/policy.rego <<'REGO'
package release

default allow := false
allow if {
  input.action == "read"
  input.user in data.release.readers
}
REGO
printf '%s\n' '{"revision":"release-1","roots":["release"],"rego_version":1}' > /opt/opa-workshop/q9/src/.manifest
opa build --bundle /opt/opa-workshop/q9/src --output /opt/opa-workshop/q9/bundle.tar.gz

checks.description: Root-scoped release-1 artifact activates and serves correct decisions

explanation: Bundle roots govern namespace ownership, revision identifies the artifact, and rego_version declares language semantics. HTTP transfer success is not activation evidence. See https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/management-bundles

title: Recover from a failed bundle activation
instructions: Systemd unit `opa001-q10` runs OPA on `127.0.0.1:18190` with `/opt/opa-workshop/q10/config.yaml`. Its configured artifact downloads but fails compilation. Inspect `sudo journalctl -u opa001-q10` and `http://127.0.0.1:18888/events/status/q10`. Recover using the immutable, supplied known-good artifact at resource `bundles/stable.tar.gz`, revision `known-good`, owning root recovery. Configure exactly one bundle named `stable`, with service workshop, retaining status reporting to status/q10, then restart the unit. Do not edit either supplied artifact. The recovered `data.recovery.allow` must allow read and deny other/missing actions; the stable bundle must activate as known-good with no activation error. Editing policy via the management API is not recovery of the bundle.
steps: Distinguish the reported compilation failure from network failure.
Replace the broken bundle configuration with stable.
Restart and verify the active revision and decisions.
solution:
cat > /opt/opa-workshop/q10/config.yaml <<'YAML'
services:
  workshop:
    url: http://127.0.0.1:18888
bundles:
  stable:
    service: workshop
    resource: bundles/stable.tar.gz
    polling: {min_delay_seconds: 1, max_delay_seconds: 2}
status:
  service: workshop
  partition_name: q10
  console: true
YAML
sudo systemctl restart opa001-q10

checks.description: Known-good stable bundle replaces the failed update and actually activates

explanation: OPA separately downloads, validates, and activates bundles. Recovery requires observing usable runtime state, not merely changing a URL. Immutable artifacts make rollback reproducible. See https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/management-status

title: Remove credentials before decision-log export
instructions: Systemd unit `opa001-q11` runs OPA at `127.0.0.1:18191`, loading `/opt/opa-workshop/q11/policy.rego`, `mask.rego`, and config.yaml. Keep the existing logging.allow business policy and enabled decision-log export. Implement `data.system.log.mask` in mask.rego so exported logs remove `/input/authorization` and `/input/password` but retain input action and request_id, the result, decision_id, and path. Restart with `sudo systemctl restart opa001-q11`. Generate test decisions using POST /v1/data/logging/allow with an input envelope; inspect sanitized exported records at `http://127.0.0.1:18888/events/logs/q11`. Masking must affect actual newly exported events, not merely a saved example. These are fake lab credentials; never supply real secrets.
steps: Return the sensitive event paths from the masking decision.
Restart the unit and send a decision with unique request_id and fake secrets.
Verify removal in the receiver while correlation and outcome remain.
solution:
cat > /opt/opa-workshop/q11/mask.rego <<'REGO'
package system.log

mask contains "/input/authorization"
mask contains "/input/password"
REGO
sudo systemctl restart opa001-q11

checks.description: Fresh exported decisions contain useful diagnostics but no fake credentials

explanation: Masking uses decision-event paths, including the input prefix. Transport encryption alone does not protect stored credentials. Real deployments also need access/retention controls; this lab receiver is loopback-only and bounded in memory. See https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/management-decision-logs#masking-sensitive-data

title: Create a reusable required-label policy
instructions: Gatekeeper is preinstalled. Create ConstraintTemplate `opalabels`, defining kind `OPALabels`, with a structural parameter schema containing labels as an array of strings. Use Rego v1 via targets[].code[].engine Rego and source.version v1, not the legacy targets[].rego field. The policy must report a violation when any label in input.parameters.labels is absent or empty on the reviewed object. Create Constraint `require-team-owner`, enforcing deny on core/v1 ConfigMaps only in namespace opa-labels with parameters labels `["team","owner"]`. A ConfigMap with both nonempty labels must pass; either absent/empty label must fail. Do not broaden enforcement to system namespaces or other questions.
steps: Define the reusable kind and structural labels parameter schema.
Write a violation set using the parameters and reviewed object.
Apply the template, wait for its CRD, then apply the narrowly matched constraint.
solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata: {name: opalabels}
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names: {kind: OPALabels}
      validation:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            labels:
              type: array
              items: {type: string}
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    code:
    - engine: Rego
      source:
        version: v1
        rego: |
          package opalabels
          violation contains {"msg": sprintf("missing label %s", [key])} if {
            some key in input.parameters.labels
            object.get(object.get(input.review.object.metadata, "labels", {}), key, "") == ""
          }
YAML
kubectl wait --for=create crd/opalabels.constraints.gatekeeper.sh --timeout=60s
kubectl wait --for=condition=Established crd/opalabels.constraints.gatekeeper.sh --timeout=60s
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: OPALabels
metadata: {name: require-team-owner}
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
  match:
    kinds: [{apiGroups: [""], kinds: [ConfigMap]}]
    namespaces: [opa-labels]
  parameters:
    labels: [team, owner]
YAML

checks.description: Parameterized Rego v1 template and scoped constraint enforce both labels

explanation: The template defines reusable logic and parameter schema; a Constraint supplies matching and parameter values. Gatekeeper v1 syntax is opted into through the code engine source, separately from the standalone OPA runtime. See https://open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper/website/docs/constrainttemplates/

title: Repair matching and identify an existing violation
instructions: Existing Constraint `audit-env` of kind `OPAAuditLabels` should require nonempty env on ConfigMaps in namespace opa-audit, but its matching excludes that namespace. Repair the Constraint, keeping enforcementAction deny, the env parameter, and scope limited to ConfigMaps in opa-audit. Preserve preexisting ConfigMap legacy without adding the missing label: the exercise is to observe, not remediate, this historical violation. Wait for audit, then write `/opt/opa-workshop/q13/audit.json` containing exactly `{"namespace":"opa-audit","name":"legacy"}`. The grader checks the live audit status and admission behavior as well as that identification. Audit interval is 10 seconds. Do not change the independent q12 template.
steps: Inspect namespaces and excludedNamespaces in the Constraint.
Remove the contradictory exclusion.
Read status.violations and identify the legacy ConfigMap.

checks.description: Correct matching enforces new requests and audit reports the preserved legacy violation

explanation: Exclusions narrow matching even when a namespace is positively included. Admission evaluates new requests; audit reports already-stored resources and does not retroactively reject or repair them. See https://open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper/website/docs/audit/

title: Synchronize referenced Namespace data
instructions: Existing Rego v1 template `opanamespaceteam` and Constraint `namespace-team` check ConfigMap label team against its Namespace label using `data.inventory.cluster["v1"].Namespace`. Missing inventory deliberately denies. Repair Gatekeeper Config `config` in namespace gatekeeper-system to synchronize core/v1 Namespace resources. Preserve the supplied policy and enforcement scope: only ConfigMaps in opa-inventory-blue and opa-inventory-green. Those Namespaces have team blue and green respectively. After synchronization, matching nonempty team labels must pass and mismatches/missing labels must fail in both namespaces. Do not replace the referential comparison with hard-coded namespace names, disable the constraint, or change Namespace labels.
steps: Add Namespace to spec.sync.syncOnly on the Gatekeeper Config.
Allow inventory time to converge.
Test matching and mismatched ConfigMaps in both namespaces.

checks.description: Namespace inventory is enabled and referential admission works in both tenant namespaces

explanation: Constraint matching does not populate inventory. Referenced kinds need synchronization, whose local view is eventually consistent rather than an atomic cluster snapshot. See https://open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper/website/docs/sync/

title: Gate Terraform plan JSON and lint Rego
instructions: In `/opt/opa-workshop/q15/policy/main.rego`, implement Conftest package main with deny messages for resource_changes entries where type is aws_s3_bucket and change.after.acl is public-read or public-read-write. Private buckets, unrelated resource types, and an empty plan must pass. Preserve supplied public.json/private.json; use `conftest test --policy /opt/opa-workshop/q15/policy FILE`. Separately fix assignment-operator lint findings in q15/lint.rego, preserving `data.lint.allow` (read true, other/missing actions false). Required lint command: `regal lint --disable-all --enable use-assignment-operator /opt/opa-workshop/q15/lint.rego`. Only this selected lint rule is assessed; lint success does not replace behavioral checks.
steps: Iterate actual plan resource_changes, not Terraform source syntax.
Report only the two public ACLs on S3 buckets.
Use := in rule assignments and verify behavior separately.
solution:
cat > /opt/opa-workshop/q15/policy/main.rego <<'REGO'
package main

deny contains sprintf("public bucket %v", [i]) if {
  some i, resource in input.resource_changes
  resource.type == "aws_s3_bucket"
  resource.change.after.acl in {"public-read", "public-read-write"}
}
REGO
cat > /opt/opa-workshop/q15/lint.rego <<'REGO'
package lint

default allow := false
allow := true if input.action == "read"
REGO

checks.description: Conftest rejects only specified public bucket ACLs and Regal-selected lint passes without semantic regression

explanation: Conftest evaluates structured configuration, while Regal analyzes Rego source. A Terraform plan's JSON shape differs from source configuration. Neither linting nor a successful build proves authorization correctness. See https://www.conftest.dev/ and https://www.openpolicyagent.org/projects/regal/

title: Optimize a representative lookup without weakening policy
instructions: In `/opt/opa-workshop/q16/policy.rego`, implement Boolean `data.q16.allow`: read only, with input.tenant equal to the trusted tenant of input.resource, unknown/missing resources denied. Preserve q16/data.json and input.json. data.json contains equivalent list `records` and keyed object `inventory` for 4,000 documents. The baseline `/opt/painkiller/opa001/testing/slow.rego` scans records. Use the keyed representation to reduce evaluation work while preserving decisions. Save JSON artifacts q16/profile.json from `opa eval --profile --format=json --data policy.rego --data data.json --input input.json data.q16.allow` and q16/bench.json from `opa bench --format=json --count=1 --benchmem --data policy.rego --data data.json --input input.json data.q16.allow`. Run from q16 or use absolute paths. Grading compares freshly profiled expression-evaluation counts with the supplied baseline and tests positive, denied, and missing-field cases; there is no wall-clock speed threshold.
steps: Replace the full list scan with data.inventory[input.resource].
Retain action, tenant, and default-deny requirements.
Generate profile/benchmark JSON on the supplied representative workload and test boundary inputs.
solution:
cat > /opt/opa-workshop/q16/policy.rego <<'REGO'
package q16

default allow := false
allow if {
  input.action == "read"
  input.tenant == data.inventory[input.resource].tenant
}
REGO
cd /opt/opa-workshop/q16
opa eval --profile --format=json --data policy.rego --data data.json --input input.json data.q16.allow > profile.json
opa bench --format=json --count=1 --benchmem --data policy.rego --data data.json --input input.json data.q16.allow > bench.json

checks.description: Keyed lookup preserves decisions, reduces measured evaluation work, and includes profile/benchmark evidence

explanation: Representative profiles identify actual work; benchmarks measure cost under recorded conditions. Deterministic expression counts avoid grading host load. Optimization is unacceptable if a missing ownership field becomes allow. See https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/policy-performance
